subject.declared_domain: the canonical keep-dormant registry -- the dormant-vs-dead guard's lookup source, whose four required fields the D3 lifecycle axis adopts verbatim

methodology.evidence: Parsed at HEAD: {schema_version:1, revalidation_default_days:180, discriminators (4), entries (7)}. Hand-authored, git-reviewed. Its own RULING 1 states the YAML is canonical and an opal:lifecycle AWS tag is an optional projected mirror that LOSES on conflict, because a tag is not in git history.
methodology.how: A registry of DELIBERATE dormancy. Its stated reason for existing is that a deliberate belt and a corpse are identical on every mechanical signal -- both DISABLED, both 0-invocation, both 0-consumer -- and only an INTENT ANNOTATION separates them. It COMPOSES nothing and INVENTS the intent schema and decay rule.

invents.note: reason + rearm_condition + annotation_cite + revalidate_by, all required per RULING 2
an entry past revalidate_by is STALE and demands human re-grounding; STALE never auto-promotes to DEBT

declared_opinions: revalidation_default_days = 180 -- a chosen decay window, not a derived one
the FAIL-SAFE DEFAULT: a resource tripping only mechanical Tier-C signals defaults to KEEP-DORMANT and never to DEBT, a deliberate bias against reaping
the 4 hand-enumerated discriminators that decide belt-vs-corpse

key.evidence: Keys are resource_id strings of the form '<type>:<name>'. Measured shapes across the 7: event_rule:, ssm_parameter:, lever:, ec2_instance:, secret_version:. NOT ARNs. ⛔ CROSSES SPACES: an AWS-native consumer holds ARNs, this registry holds a hand-written type:name grammar, and NO MAPPING IS DECLARED. The 'lever:' prefix is not an AWS resource type at all -- it names a manual procedure, so that member cannot carry an ARN even in principle, which means the crossing is not merely undeclared but partial by construction.
key.key_expression: a member is an element of $.entries[*]; key = .resource_id, of the form <type>:<name>

failure_mode.evidence: EXERCISED, both arms reachable from different truths in one run: a membership test for 'arn:aws:lambda:zzz' returns bare False; the control test for a real id 'event_rule:inf-gold-incremental-daily' returns True. ⛔ THE FAILURE MODE IS THAT A MISS IS A VERDICT, NOT AN ERROR. Absent-from-registry MEANS not-deliberately-dormant, i.e. DEBT-eligible. So a mistyped or wrong-grammar id returns the SAME False as a genuine absence, and the guard cannot distinguish 'this resource is not belted' from 'you spelled it wrong'. Given the id space is hand-authored and crosses to ARN space with no declared mapping, a spelling miss is not a hypothetical.
failure_mode.returns_on_failure: bare False, read by the guard as NOT-keep-dormant and therefore DEBT-eligible
silent_degrade_paths: a mistyped resource_id makes a genuinely belted resource read as DEBT-eligible
an entry past revalidate_by still returns True and keeps protecting, so the decay rule does not fail closed

verdict.why: The DESIGN is unusually strong and this verdict is not about the design: the file exists precisely because a belt and a corpse are mechanically identical, it demands grounded reasons, and it carries its own decay rule. It is UNSOUND on TRUST. Three measured facts compound: a lookup miss is indistinguishable from a mistyped id AND is consumed as a DEBT-eligible verdict; the id space crosses to ARNs with declared_mapping NULL and one member cannot have an ARN at all; and the decay rule the file itself defines is already breached by 1 of its 7 entries with nothing scheduled that could ever raise it.
blocking_defects: 1 of 7 entries past its own revalidate_by, with no scheduled re-grounding
a lookup miss is a VERDICT (DEBT-eligible), indistinguishable from a mistyped id
id space crosses to ARN space with declared_mapping NULL
